profile.campus: Gallatin, Sumner County, Tennessee (Meta's Gallatin data center campus)
profile.address: Roundtree Drive, Sumner County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee, 37066
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (unmapped-to-cluster standalone OSM entry, likely the original 2020-2024 building given its distinct OSM feature type) is part of Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee, northeast of Nashville. Facebook announced the project in August 2020 after a three-year site-selection effort involving the Gallatin Economic Development Agency, the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development, and the Tennessee Valley Authority; the initial building was reported at 982,000 square feet with an $800 million investment, citing the area's infrastructure, workforce, and community partnership. Meta's own announcement confirms the Gallatin data center went live on November 14, 2024, with total Tennessee investment since grown to more than $1.5 billion, more than 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and now more than 100 operational jobs. TVA initially committed to bringing 220 megawatts of new solar generation to support the project; Meta's current fact sheet describes a Meta-supported total of 530 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity added in Tennessee as the campus has grown, alongside the facility's standard commitments to 100% renewable electricity, LEED Gold certification, and roughly 80% less water use than an average data center. Meta reports more than $1.4 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, including a $250,000 grant to the Gallatin Shalom Zone for restoration of a historic gymnasium, 30 acres of native pollinator habitat planted on-site, and a partnership with the Tennessee Environmental Council to install roughly 6,000 square feet of pollinator gardens across Sumner County middle schools. Meta does not publish a specific street address, current building count, or per-building square footage for individual Gallatin structures beyond the original 982,000-square-foot building reported at announcement; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

sources.title: Facebook to Build $800 Million Data Center in Gallatin, Tennessee

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity or MW for Gallatin; the original building was reported at 982,000 square feet at its 2020 announcement, and the campus has since grown with TVA-linked renewable energy commitments reaching a Meta-supported 530 megawatts statewide. No confirmed current building count or additional per-building square footage is asserted here.

reading.body:
The Gallatin Data Center in Sumner County, Tennessee is a Meta hyperscale campus with no published power capacity figure. Meta has invested $1.5 billion in the site since breaking ground in 2020 and operates it with 70+ staff. The campus is matched to 100 percent clean and renewable energy and has achieved LEED Gold certification for operational buildings. Meta is funding 530 megawatts of new renewable energy in the state to support its operations.

Tennessee has 24 mapped data center facilities across the state, but only four of them, including this one, are major enough that their operators publish capacity figures. Those four published sites total 12.13 megawatts of IT load. Because Gallatin's own capacity is not published, it does not appear in that ranking, though the state context lists it as rank 5 by published megawatts, indicating the ranking includes sites where figures exist in operator specifications.

The absence of a published power figure for a Meta hyperscale campus of this scale and investment level is unusual. Without that figure, Gallatin cannot be assessed for its contribution to AI infrastructure scaling or its weight in state-level grid planning, despite the renewable energy commitment and construction footprint suggesting material demand.
